newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh port blockade protest ends.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh port blockade protest ends.

text.p: A day-long blockade of Bangladesh's main Chittagong port by lorry drivers was called off on Tuesday evening, port officials said.
Cargo handling at the port was suspended after the drivers blockaded jetties early on Tuesday to protest against the death of a transport worker.
The worker, Abdul Wahab Noman, was killed when iron pipes rolled on him as he took a nap on one of the jetties on Monday night.
Angry protesters parked their trucks on the road leading to the jetties.
The Chittagong Port Authority (CPA), which described Noman's death as an accident, later agreed to pay 50,000 taka ($1,150) in compensation to Noman's family.
"The compensation deal led to the end of the blockade," one CPA official said.
There were 19 ships at the jetties and eight at the outer anchorage awaiting loading, unloading and berths on Tuesday. Over 100,000 tonnes of cargo and 11,861 containers were piled up at the port.
